P = {}
P["s1"] = ("1. Question and configurations. How much do scaling and PCA change a terrain map built from eight sensors, "
           "and does a 3-cluster k-means classifier that borrows terrain names from 60 labels match 1-NN? Table 1 compares "
           "six configurations: scaling (raw or z-score) and model (k-means or 1-NN) on all 8 sensors, then PCA keeping 95% "
           "of the variance on the z-scored sensors for both models, so neighbors differ in one factor. My k-means follows "
           "ISL Algorithm 12.2 in NumPy: a random cluster for every point, then centroids and nearest-centroid "
           "reassignment until no label changes (cap 300 iterations), keeping the best of 10 random starts by "
           "within-cluster sum of squares. An empty cluster would be re-seeded at the farthest point; none occurred. Each "
           "cluster takes the majority label of the 60 calibration-training points, which was one-to-one every time. Three "
           "clusters match the three terrains and the elbow agrees (objective 2652, 1238, 1086 for k = 2, 3, 4).")
P["s2"] = ("2. Evaluation protocol. Normalization, PCA and k-means were fitted on the 754 fit rows (all practice rows except "
           "the 30 validation rows; no labels). The 60 calibration-training labels (20 per terrain) named clusters and "
           "trained 1-NN. Every configuration was scored on the same 30 validation rows (10 per terrain; one error is 3.3 "
           "points). I selected the model on these rows, so its score is a selection score, not a test score, and the "
           "practice run shows deployment, not accuracy. Mission rows were transformed with the stored mean, standard "

# Homework - 2
## Overview
Rover Rescue (CSCI 4521 HW2): build a terrain classifier from eight sensors (firm, rough, sand), compare scaling, PCA and k-means against 1-NN, deploy one fitted model on the practice and mission grids, and explain the evidence in a standalone report of at most two pages. The grade is the 100-point `rubric.md` in the course repo, not the 10, 20 and 10 points printed in the PDF. No extra credit is offered in the handout, the repo markdown or the rubric.
Deadline: 11 pm on 2026-10-27, as the user stated it. Confirm on the Gradescope assignment page: the Board's schedule listed HW2 for 10/20, the handout says "check Gradescope", and the repo folder was committed 2026-10-22.
Status 2026-10-27: the notebook, both figures, `submission.csv` and the practice HTML are final and tested. Left: the Word report and its PDF, then the upload.
## Requirements
### What the handout asks for
Three design parts and four deliverables. Nothing beyond this belongs in the notebook.
- Representation: examine sensor scales, run PCA, report the component count for 95% variance, plot components against explained variance, show the top 2 and top 3 components.
- Experiments: at least three configurations that together show the effect of normalization, a PCA representation, and cluster-based against kNN. Record dimensions, validation accuracy, macro F1, sand recall and the practice outcome for each. Use k-means with three clusters, justify the cluster count and the way clusters get terrain names, and explain why missing sand matters.
- Deployment: choose one fitted model, reuse it on the practice and mission grids, show a practice deployment, export `submission.csv`, explain the choice, and analyze one failure, surprise or limitation.
- NumPy by hand: normalization, nearest-centroid assignment, centroid update, kNN prediction, and your own k-means loop.
### Submit
Upload exactly these four, from `D:\\_Anant\\10_Areas\\UMN\\Classes\\CSCI\\CSCI 4521\\Code\\Homework\\`:
- [ ] `CSCI4521_HW2.ipynb`, saved with outputs (code and every figure used in the report)
- [ ] `practice_run.html`, the practice deployment animation (the same run appears as a static map in Figure 2 of the report)
- [ ] `submission.csv`, from `save_submission`, 784 rows in mission.csv order, `student_id` demo3 (the instructor says to leave it)
- [ ] the report PDF (export from Word, two pages at most)
Do not upload: the `rover-rescue-download/` folder (it holds the dataset and `practice_truth.bin`), the starter notebook `[REDACTED].ipynb`, `figures/` files as separate items, or any HW1 file.
How: Gradescope, CSCI 4521, Homework 2, upload. Whether the page has one multi-file slot or four slots is unverified, so read the page first. After uploading, open each file in the Gradescope preview and keep the confirmation.
### Must not do
- Do not read `practice_truth.bin`; only `evaluate_practice` and `show_practice_run` touch it.
- Do not change `split_data` or its split.
- Do not use x, y as features.
- Do not fit normalization, PCA or k-means on validation rows, and never fit anything on mission data.
- Do not use validation labels to name clusters or train 1-NN.
- Do not replace the four required NumPy operations with library versions.
- Do not call the validation score an untouched test estimate, or the practice run an accuracy estimate.
### Report must state
- [ ] Question, the configurations compared and why.
- [ ] The component count for 95% variance.
- [ ] What scaling and PCA changed and what cluster versus kNN showed, tied to the metrics. A tie is reported as a tie.
- [ ] Why the deployed model was chosen, how a missed sand cell changes the route, and one failure, surprise, tie or limitation.
- [ ] Which rows were used for fitting, naming and validation, and how the fitted model was reused on mission.
- [ ] Observations kept apart from explanations. The AI-use note sits at the bottom.
### Rules

## Work log
### 2026-10-27 Final state and tests
`Code\\Homework\\CSCI4521_HW2.ipynb` has 39 cells: the 8 starter cells unchanged, then eight short sections (setup, NumPy methods, checks, representation, experiments, selection, deployment, export), a summary and an AI-use note. About 415 words of prose in total, two report figures plus the practice animation, and nothing else drawn. k-means follows ISL Algorithm 12.2 and lecture 2.3. Code style follows the CSCI 4041 projects: a docstring with time cost on every function, comments on each step, and assert-based checks.
Trimmed to what the handout asks for, after the user pointed out the notebook was doing too much:
- Six configurations instead of eleven: raw and z-score, k-means and 1-NN on all 8 sensors, then PCA at 95% on the standardized sensors for both models. Dropped: raw-data PCA configurations, PCA with 2 components, 3-NN.
- PCA is fitted on the standardized sensors only. Dropped: the raw PCA curve and count, the loadings table.
- Dropped: the 20-start stability test, the elbow plot (the four objective values stay as one line), the mission-shift table and shares, the timing columns, the kNN closure, the drawing function and its tests.
- Kept: everything the three parts and the rubric name, plus the checks.
Tests run, all on the final file in the user's `csci-4521` env (Python 3.12.14, numpy 2.5.3, pandas 3.0.6, scikit-learn 1.9.1, matplotlib 3.11.2):
- The user re-ran the earlier 28-cell version in that env and its outputs were byte-identical to my Python 3.14 runs, so results do not depend on the environment. The trimmed final file ran in that env in a clean directory (12.8 seconds) and in place: no error or stderr output, execution counts 1 to 25 in order, and the two runs produced byte-identical `submission.csv`, results table and figures.
- Three check cells, all assert-based. A general block: fit and validation rows are disjoint, grid order is row-major, z-score has mean 0 and std 1, vectorized distances equal the lecture 1.1 loop and kNN for k = 1, 3, 5 equals a loop reference on raw and z-scored data, k-means clusters partition the data and converge with a non-increasing objective and centroids equal to member means, the best random start is kept, PCA components are orthonormal and its variance equals the squared singular values, and sklearn agrees (k-means objective 1237.50 in both, standardization, macro F1, accuracy). A unit block with a hand-worked case for every method (constant sensor, 3-4-5 triangle, empty-cluster re-seed, within-cluster sum, exact recovery of three blobs, the iteration cap, naming by majority and by the one-to-one fallback, the nearest-neighbor tie-break, and the lecture 1.4 COVID example: precision 0.5, recall 0.75, F1 0.6, accuracy 0.8). A pipeline block: stored z-score and PCA, repeatable fits, every table value against sklearn accuracy and a direct sand recall.
- Coverage (coverage.py on the executed notebook): the check cells alone run 207 of 207 lines and 22 of 22 branches of my code, with all 16 functions fully covered. The whole notebook runs 366 of 366 lines and 40 of 40 branches.
- Mutation test: 14 deliberate bugs (distance sign flipped, argmin to argmax, wrong centroid divisor, dropped square, convergence never detected, worst start kept, worst naming permutation, transposed table, neighbors ordered farthest first, F1 without the factor 2, sand recall read from the wrong class, and others). The checks caught all 14. An earlier round caught 13; the survivor ("keep the worst random start") exposed a missing check, which the raw-features best-start check now covers.
- Defect found by the checks while building them: ties in the empty-cluster re-seed were broken by an unstable sort. Fixed with a stable sort. No run ever had an empty cluster, so no result changed.
- Fact-check: a script compares 41 statements of the report (every number in the text, the cluster tables, the elbow values, the selection tie, the practice outcome, each Table 1 row) with the executed notebook output and the results CSV. All 41 match.
- pyflakes finds no unused names or imports in my cells, pycodestyle at 120 columns is clean, no stderr output anywhere, no em or en dashes.
- Layout estimate with PyMuPDF (Times 11 pt, 0.75 in margins, the real figure files, page break before Table 1): 2 pages, page 2 ends at about 85% of its height, Table 1 whole on page 2.
What "100%" does and does not mean: the code is verified correct and reproducible, and the report numbers are verified against the output. The grade itself cannot be verified. The validation score is 1.000 for four of six configurations on only 30 rows, which says nothing certain about the hidden mission labels, and the handout says no points depend on them.
Not tested: Word itself, the Gradescope upload, and a Colab run.
Evidence (demo bundle, the confirmed dataset):
- Split: fit 754, calibration-training 60 (20 per class), validation 30 (10 per class).
- Scales: std runs from 0.040 (sensor_6) to 52.4 (sensor_4), a ratio of 1,320. Sensors 4 and 2 supply 92.27% of raw squared distance.
- PCA on the standardized fit rows: 95% needs 3 components (cumulative 0.9546; PC1 64.1%, PC2 27.1%, first two 91.1%). Three separated groups show in PC1 and PC2.
- Raw k-means: validation accuracy 0.700, macro F1 0.704, sand recall 0.5 (5 of 10), rover stuck at step 20 at (y=13, x=4) where it predicted rough. The cluster named sand holds 12 sand, 11 rough and 4 firm training points. Raw 1-NN: 0.933, 0.935, sand recall 0.9, reaches the goal (cost 72.2).
- All four z-scored configurations (8 sensors and PCA 95%, k-means and 1-NN) score 1.000 on accuracy, macro F1 and sand recall and reach the goal in 54 steps at cost 70.8. Their clusters are pure on the 60 training labels (20, 20, 20).
- The pre-set rule (macro F1, then sand recall, then fewer dimensions, then table order) picked C5 (z-score, PCA 95%, k-means, 3 dimensions), tied with C6 on every metric.
- Elbow objective: k=2 2652, k=3 1238, k=4 1086, k=5 939. Mission route cost 52.0.
### Decisions
- Word, not LaTeX: two pages, one table, two figures, no equations, no bibliography. Switch only if the table cannot fit.
- Figures are saved at print size (7.25 in and 5.34 in wide at 300 dpi) so that text stays readable when inserted at full width.
- The `BUNDLE_OVERRIDE` cell was removed after the Piazza answer.
- Selection rule fixed before any result: macro F1, then sand recall, then fewer dimensions, then table order. The practice outcome is recorded, not used to select.
- The notebook stores a generic `python3` kernel name so any Jupyter or Colab opens it without a missing-kernel prompt.
### Rubric coverage
"Met" means the evidence exists in the executed notebook, not that points are guaranteed.
| Rubric line | Where | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Learning system and method choices (25) | notebook 2 Methods, 5 Experiments | z-score, nearest-centroid, centroid update, own k-means loop, cluster naming from the 60 labels, kNN, all NumPy; initialization, stopping rule and empty clusters stated and counted |
| Sensor scales (4) | notebook 4, first table | std range 1,320x, share of raw squared distance per sensor |
| PCA and 95% count (6) | notebook 4, PCA cell | fitted on fit rows only, 3 components |
| PCA figure and reading (5) | `figures/fig1_pca.png`, report 3 | variance curve, top 2 and top 3 components |
| Three or more configurations (8) | notebook 5 | six configurations, one factor changed at a time |
| Common held-out evaluation, boundaries (9) | notebook 1 Setup, 5 | asserts, same 30 validation rows, labels only for naming and 1-NN |
| Dimensions, accuracy, macro F1, sand recall, practice (8) | notebook 5 table, `figures/hw2_configs.csv`, Table 1 | all five per configuration |
| Model choice, reuse, mission map, practice run (10) | notebook 6 and 7, `practice_run.html`, `figures/fig2_deploy.png` | rule fixed first, stored objects reused, mission map and route |
| Report (20) | Word report | draft below: question, table, figures, sand risk, protocol, limitations |
| Reproducibility (5) | notebook header and Summary | dependencies, run steps, seed, versions, clean-directory run verified |
### Word report layout
The two-page limit is the one rubric line that cannot be verified until Word runs, so follow these settings from the start.
- Page: Letter, 0.75 in margins, one column. Times New Roman 11 pt, single spacing, 3 pt after paragraphs, 0 before, body justified.
- Optional page header (HW1 used one): `CSCI 4521`, tab, `Anant Gupta`, tab, `October 27, 2026`, 9 pt, bottom border.
- Title block: three centered bold lines, `HW 2: Rover Rescue`, `Anant Gupta`, `October 2026`.
- Each numbered paragraph starts with its title in bold (`1. Question and configurations.`), then the text in normal weight.
- Order: title block, sections 1 and 2, section 3 first paragraph, Figure 1, section 3 second paragraph, a page break, Table 1, section 4, Figure 2, section 5, the AI-use line.
- Figure 1: `figures/fig1_pca.png`, Insert, Pictures, In Line with Text, centered, 7.0 in wide with the aspect ratio locked. Caption below, 10 pt, centered.
- Figure 2: `figures/fig2_deploy.png`, same way, 5.3 in wide.
- Table 1: paste the tab-separated block below, Insert, Table, Convert Text to Table with 8 columns. 9 pt, header row bold with a rule above and below, light rule under each row, text columns left, number columns centered, caption below.
- Copy the text from source mode (Ctrl+E in Obsidian) and use Paste Special, Unformatted Text. Remove the bracketed notes.
- Export: File, Save As, PDF (Standard). Reopen the PDF and check: two pages, page 2 ends with the AI-use line and about an inch or more of space, text is selectable, both figures are sharp and their labels readable, Table 1 sits whole on page 2.
- If it spills past two pages, do these in order and stop when it fits: Figure 2 to 4.3 in, body to 10.5 pt, margins to 0.7 in, drop the elbow numbers from section 1. Never cut the protocol, the sand-risk paragraph, the limitations or Table 1; the rubric scores them.

## Overview
Rover Rescue (CSCI 4521 HW2): build a terrain classifier from eight sensors (firm, rough, sand), compare scaling, PCA and k-means against 1-NN, deploy one fitted model on the practice and mission grids, and explain the evidence in a standalone report of at most two pages. ### Report length: two pages, not more

The rubric's report line (20 points) ends with "Maximum two pages." So do not extend to three or four pages and do not add diagrams. The example `HW2.pdf` is 8 pages because it answers an older assignment with no limit; use it for tone and layout only. If a longer report is wanted anyway, ask the instructor on Piazza first; the written rubric is what a grader follows.
### What the handout asks for
Three design parts and four deliverables. Nothing beyond this belongs in the notebook.
- Representation: examine sensor scales, run PCA, report the component count for 95% variance, plot components against explained variance, show the top 2 and top 3 components.
- Experiments: at least three configurations that together show the effect of normalization, a PCA representation, and cluster-based against kNN. Record dimensions, validation accuracy, macro F1, sand recall and the practice outcome for each. Use k-means with three clusters, justify the cluster count and the way clusters get terrain names, and explain why missing sand matters.
- Deployment: choose one fitted model, reuse it on the practice and mission grids, show a practice deployment, export `submission.csv`, explain the choice, and analyze one failure, surprise or limitation.
- NumPy by hand: normalization, nearest-centroid assignment, centroid update, kNN prediction, and your own k-means loop.

<pasted_content id="6aca">
HW 2: Rover Rescue

Anant Gupta October 2026

1. Question and Configurations

How much change occurs when we scale the data and do PCA? Does a 3 cluster k-means using the names of the terrains from the 60 labels perform as well as 1-NN? Table 1 shows 6 configurations. All the configurations include scaling (raw data or z-score) and using all 8 sensors. The final 2 configurations only include the PCA version of the z-scored data, including all 8 sensors but reducing dimensionality to keep 95% variance. This means the neighbors only vary in 1 factor. I have implemented k-means using ISL Algorithm 12.2 using NumPy. Each point has a random cluster assigned. The centroids are calculated, and the points are assigned to the closest centroid. This is repeated until no labels have been changed (maximum of 300 iterations). This gives the best result from 10 random starts based on the within cluster sum of squares. If any clusters are empty they will be re-seeded with the farthest point, however, there were none. The majority class from the 60 labelled calibration training points is assigned to the clusters. In every case, this was 1:1. The number of clusters is 3, meaning there are 3 clusters for the 3 terrains. The elbow matches (objective 2652, 1238, 1086 for k = 2, 3, 4).

2. Evaluation

The normalisation, PCA and k-means were fit on the 754 rows of fit data (all practice data excluding the 30 validation rows). The 60 labelled calibration training rows were used to label the clusters and train the 1-NN. The scoring was performed on the same 30 validation rows (10 per terrain). These were used to choose the model, meaning this score represents the selection score rather than the test score. The practice data was run to show how it would perform during deployment. The mission data was transformed using the saved mean, standard deviation and PCA but was not fit.

3. Evidence

The standard deviations of the sensor data varies from 0.040 (sensor_6) to 52.4 (sensor_4). This is a large difference of a factor of 1320. Sensors 4 and 2 make up 92.3% of the squared distance in the raw data. The PCA reduces the data to 3 components (95.5%) while keeping 95% variance in the z-scored fit data. PC1 and PC2 group the data into 3 groups corresponding to the labelled terrains (Figure 1b).

Figure 1: (a) Cumulative explained variance (b) PC1 and PC2 (c) PC1-PC3 of z-scored fit data. Fit data shown in grey. Training data shown in colour.

The scaling had the biggest impact. Using the same model and representation, the z-scored data increased the accuracy of the k-means model from 0.700 to 1.000. The 1-NN also increased from 0.933 to 1.000. Without the scaling, the k-means had an accuracy of only 5/10 in the validation data. This meant the cluster for sand contained 12 sand, 11 rough and 4 firm. However, all the clusters were pure after the z-scoring (20, 20, 20). The PCA made no difference as both models achieved a score of 1.000 for the 3 component data. Both the cluster and 1-NN had a score of 1.000 for all the z-scored configurations. For the raw data, the 1-NN performed better than the k-means (0.933 vs 0.700). This may be because the raw data is split mainly on sensor_4.

Table 1: Number of dimensions, accuracy, macro F1 (average of 3 class F1 scores), sand recall and the predicted result for the rover on practice data.

4. Conclusion and Risk of Sand

There are 4 tied configurations with an accuracy, macro F1 and sand recall of 1.000 (C3, C4, C5, C6). Therefore, these cannot be ordered based on the validation. My criteria was to select the model with the highest macro F1, then sand recall, then fewest dimensions and finally the order in the table. This meant C5 was the chosen model (z-score, 95% PCA, k-means, 3 dimensions). This only differs from C6 due to the order in the table, so there was a tie. The practice data performed well with a successful route in 54 steps. The predicted cost was 70.8 which was the same as the other 3 (Figure 2). The sand cells that were not detected were predicted as firm or rough, meaning the planner thinks they can be passed through. The rover will stop the first time it passes through this cell. Only 1 cell was blocked by the raw k-means as it predicted 5 of the 10 sand cells as rough. The rover stopped on step 20 at (y=13, x=4). The model predicted rough but the simulator said it was sand. 1-NN also failed to detect 1 sand cell out of the 10 validation data but still achieved its goal.

Figure 2: Chosen model C5. Left: Practice data map with planned route (Mission successful in 54 steps). Right: Predicted mission map with planned route.

5. Limitations

The 30 validation rows were not enough to differentiate between the 4 perfect models. A perfect score on the validation data does not mean it is a perfect model. Only 1 successful route was found on the practice data. There are no labels on the mission data meaning I cannot see how well the model generalises to the new area.

def table_rows():
    df = pd.read_csv(f"{H}/figures/hw2_configs.csv")
    rows = []
    for _, r in df.iterrows():
        outcome = f"stuck, step {int(r.steps)}" if "STUCK" in r.practice else f"success, {int(r.steps)} steps"
        rows.append([r.config, r.scaling, f"{r.representation} ({int(r.dims)})", r.model,
                     f"{r.val_accuracy:.3f}", f"{r.macro_f1:.3f}", f"{r.sand_recall:.2f}", outcome])
    return rows

        if k != "title":
            parts.append(v)
    return " ".join(parts)

    th { border-top: 0.8pt solid #000; border-bottom: 0.8pt solid #000; }
    div.c { text-align: center; margin: 2pt 0 0 0; }

    head_html = "<tr>" + "".join(f"<th>{c}</th>" for c in HEAD) + "</tr>"
    BRK = "" if os.environ.get("BREAK") == "0" else "page-break-before: always"

    def sec(h, *paras):
        return f'<p class="h">{P[h]}</p>' + "".join(f"<p>{P[k]}</p>" for k in paras)

    FIG1 = f"""<div class="c"><img src="fig1_pca.png" width="504"></div><p class="cap">{P['f1cap']}</p>"""

    story = fitz.Story(html=html, user_css=css, archive=fitz.Archive(f"{H}/figures"))
    writer = fitz.DocumentWriter(OUT)

    while more:
        dev = writer.begin_page(mediabox)
        more, filled = story.place(where)
        story.draw(dev)
        writer.end_page()
        pages += 1
        last_bottom = filled[3]
    writer.close()
    print(f"pages: {pages}; last page content ends at {100 * (last_bottom - where.y0) / (where.y1 - where.y0):.0f}% of its usable height")
    print("words in text and captions:", len(all_text().split()))

           "clusters is 3, meaning there are 3 clusters for the 3 terrains. The elbow matches (within cluster sum of "
           "squares 2652, 1238, 1086 for k = 2, 3, 4).")

P["h2"] = "2. Evaluation"
P["s2"] = ("The normalisation, PCA and k-means were fit on the 754 rows of fit data (all practice data excluding the 30 "
           "validation rows). The 60 labelled calibration training rows were used to label the clusters and train the "
           "1-NN. The scoring of every configuration was performed on the same 30 validation rows (10 per terrain). These "
           "were used to choose the model, meaning this score represents the selection score rather than the test score. "
           "The practice data was run to show how the model would perform during deployment, which is a demonstration "
           "and not an accuracy estimate. The mission data was transformed using the saved mean, standard deviation and "
           "PCA but was not fit.")

P["h3"] = "3. Evidence"
P["s3a"] = ("The standard deviations of the sensor data vary from 0.040 (sensor_6) to 52.4 (sensor_4). This is a large "
            "difference of a factor of 1320. Sensors 4 and 2 make up 92.3% of the squared distance in the raw data. The PCA "
            "reduces the z-scored fit data to 3 components, which keep 95.5% of the variance, so 3 components are needed "
            "for 95% (Figure 1a). PC1 and PC2 group the data into 3 groups corresponding to the labelled terrains "
            "(Figure 1b).")
P["f1cap"] = ("Figure 1: (a) Cumulative explained variance (b) PC1 and PC2 (c) PC1-PC3 of z-scored fit data. Fit data shown "
              "in grey. Labelled training data shown in colour.")
P["s3b"] = ("The scaling had the biggest impact. Using the same model and representation, the z-scored data increased the "
            "accuracy of the k-means model from 0.700 to 1.000. The 1-NN also increased from 0.933 to 1.000. Without the "
            "scaling, the k-means found only 5 of the 10 sand cells in the validation data. The cluster named sand "
            "contained 12 sand, 11 rough and 4 firm labelled training points. However, all the clusters were pure after "
            "the z-scoring (20, 20, 20). The PCA made no difference as both models achieved a score of 1.000 for the 3 "
            "component data, the same as with all 8 sensors. Both the cluster and 1-NN had a score of 1.000 for all the "
            "z-scored configurations. For the raw data, the 1-NN performed better than the k-means (0.933 vs 0.700). This "
            "may be because the k-means on raw data splits mainly on sensor_4.")
P["t1cap"] = ("Table 1: Number of dimensions, validation accuracy, macro F1 (average of the 3 class F1 scores), sand recall "
              "and the result of the practice rover run for each configuration.")

P["h4"] = "4. Conclusion and Risk of Sand"
P["s4"] = ("There are 4 tied configurations with an accuracy, macro F1 and sand recall of 1.000 (C3, C4, C5, C6). "
           "Therefore, these cannot be ordered based on the validation. My criteria were to select the model with the "
           "highest macro F1, then sand recall, then fewest dimensions and finally the order in the table. This meant C5 "
           "was the chosen model (z-score, 95% PCA, k-means, 3 dimensions). This only differs from C6 due to the order in "
           "the table, so there was a tie. The practice data performed well with a successful route in 54 steps. The "
           "predicted cost was 70.8 which was the same as the other 3 tied configurations (Figure 2). The sand cells that "
           "were not detected were predicted as firm or rough, meaning the planner thinks they can be passed through. The "
           "rover will stop the first time its route passes through one of these cells. The raw k-means shows this as it "
           "predicted 5 of the 10 validation sand cells as rough. The rover stopped on step 20 at (y=13, x=4). The model "
           "predicted rough but the simulator said it was sand. The raw 1-NN also failed to detect 1 sand cell out of the "
           "10 validation sand cells but still achieved its goal, as that cell was not on its route.")
P["f2cap"] = ("Figure 2: Chosen model C5. Left: Predicted practice map with planned route (mission successful in 54 steps). "
              "Right: Predicted mission map with planned route.")

P["h5"] = "5. Limitations"
P["s5"] = ("The 30 validation rows were not enough to differentiate between the 4 perfect models. A perfect score on the "
           "validation data does not mean it is a perfect model. The practice run only tests 1 route, so it is a "
           "demonstration and not proof. There are no labels on the mission data meaning I cannot see how well the model "

P["hai"] = "AI"
P["ai"] = ("AI was allowed in this course. I used AI extensively. Claude Code (Anthropic) was used to read the course "

def table_rows():
    df = pd.read_csv(f"{H}/figures/hw2_configs.csv")
    rows = []
    for _, r in df.iterrows():
        outcome = f"stuck, step {int(r.steps)}" if "STUCK" in r.practice else f"success, {int(r.steps)} steps"
        rows.append([r.config, r.scaling, f"{r.representation} ({int(r.dims)})", r.model,
                     f"{r.val_accuracy:.3f}", f"{r.macro_f1:.3f}", f"{r.sand_recall:.2f}", outcome])
    return rows


HEAD = ["ID", "Scaling", "Representation (dims)", "Model", "Accuracy", "Macro F1", "Sand recall", "Practice rover"]
ROWS = table_rows()


def all_text():
    parts = list(P["title"])
    for k, v in P.items():
        if k != "title":
            parts.append(v)
    return " ".join(parts)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "report_est.pdf"
    css = """
    body { font-family: serif; font-size: 11pt; line-height: 1.15; }
    p { margin: 0 0 3pt 0; text-align: justify; }
    p.t { text-align: center; margin: 0; font-weight: bold; }
    p.h { text-align: left; margin: 5pt 0 2pt 0; font-weight: bold; }
    p.cap { text-align: center; font-size: 10pt; margin: 1pt 0 4pt 0; }
    table { border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 9pt; margin: 0 0 1pt 0; }
    td, th { padding: 1pt 4pt; border-bottom: 0.5pt solid #888; }
    th { border-top: 0.8pt solid #000; border-bottom: 0.8pt solid #000; }
    div.c { text-align: center; margin: 2pt 0 0 0; }
    """
    rows_html = "".join("<tr>" + "".join(f"<td>{c}</td>" for c in r) + "</tr>" for r in ROWS)
    head_html = "<tr>" + "".join(f"<th>{c}</th>" for c in HEAD) + "</tr>"
    BRK = "" if os.environ.get("BREAK") == "0" else "page-break-before: always"

    def sec(h, *paras):
        return f'<p class="h">{P[h]}</p>' + "".join(f"<p>{P[k]}</p>" for k in paras)

    FIG1 = f"""<div class="c"><img src="fig1_pca.png" width="504"></div><p class="cap">{P['f1cap']}</p>"""
    TAB = (f"""<div class="c" style="{BRK}"><table align="center">{head_html}{rows_html}</table></div>"""
           f"""<p class="cap">{P['t1cap']}</p>""")
    FIG2 = f"""<div class="c"><img src="fig2_deploy.png" width="385"></div><p class="cap">{P['f2cap']}</p>"""
    t = P["title"]
    title = (f'<p class="t">{t[0]}</p><p class="t">{t[1]}</p><p class="t" style="margin-bottom:4pt">{t[2]}</p>')
    html = (title + sec("h1", "s1") + sec("h2", "s2") + sec("h3", "s3a") + FIG1 + f"<p>{P['s3b']}</p>" + TAB
            + sec("h4", "s4") + FIG2 + sec("h5", "s5") + sec("hai", "ai"))
    story = fitz.Story(html=html, user_css=css, archive=fitz.Archive(f"{H}/figures"))
    writer = fitz.DocumentWriter(OUT)
    mediabox = fitz.paper_rect("letter")
    where = mediabox + (54, 54, -54, -54)           # 0.75 inch margins
    more, pages, last_bottom = 1, 0, 0
    while more:
        dev = writer.begin_page(mediabox)
        more, filled = story.place(where)
        story.draw(dev)
        writer.end_page()
        pages += 1
        last_bottom = filled[3]
    writer.close()
    print(f"pages: {pages}; last page content ends at {100 * (last_bottom - where.y0) / (where.y1 - where.y0):.0f}% of its usable height")
    print("words in text and captions:", len(all_text().split()))

# Homework - 2
## Overview
Rover Rescue (CSCI 4521 HW2): build a terrain classifier from eight sensors (firm, rough, sand), compare scaling, PCA and k-means against 1-NN, deploy one fitted model on the practice and mission grids, and explain the evidence in a standalone report of at most two pages. The grade is the 100-point `rubric.md` in the course repo, not the 10, 20 and 10 points printed in the PDF. No extra credit is offered in the handout, the repo markdown or the rubric.
Deadline: 11 pm on 2026-10-27, as the user stated it. Confirm on the Gradescope assignment page: the Board's schedule listed HW2 for 10/20, the handout says "check Gradescope", and the repo folder was committed 2026-10-22.
Status 2026-10-27: the notebook, both report figures, `submission.csv` and the practice HTML are final and tested. The report text is locked (the user's own wording, see Report text). Left: build the Word report and its PDF, then upload.
## Requirements
### Report length: two pages, not more
The handout calls it "the two-page report" and says "full implementation details and extra plots belong in your code/evidence, not the two-page report". The rubric's report line (20 points) ends with "Maximum two pages." So do not extend to three or four pages and do not add diagrams. The example `HW2.pdf` is 8 pages because it answers an older assignment with no limit; use it for tone and layout only. If a longer report is wanted anyway, ask the instructor on Piazza first; the written rubric is what a grader follows.
### What the handout asks for
Three design parts and four deliverables. Nothing beyond this belongs in the notebook.
- Representation: examine sensor scales, run PCA, report the component count for 95% variance, plot components against explained variance, show the top 2 and top 3 components.
- Experiments: at least three configurations that together show the effect of normalization, a PCA representation, and cluster-based against kNN. Record dimensions, validation accuracy, macro F1, sand recall and the practice outcome for each. Use k-means with three clusters, justify the cluster count and the way clusters get terrain names, and explain why missing sand matters.
- Deployment: choose one fitted model, reuse it on the practice and mission grids, show a practice deployment, export `submission.csv`, explain the choice, and analyze one failure, surprise or limitation.
- NumPy by hand: normalization, nearest-centroid assignment, centroid update, kNN prediction, and your own k-means loop.
### Submit
Upload exactly these four, from `D:\\_Anant\\10_Areas\\UMN\\Classes\\CSCI\\CSCI 4521\\Code\\Homework\\`:
- [ ] `CSCI4521_HW2.ipynb` (1.3 MB), saved with outputs
- [ ] `practice_run.html` (0.7 MB), the practice deployment animation, centered on the screen

import sys, zipfile, re
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Emu

path = sys.argv[1]
d = Document(path)
print("=====", path)
for i, s in enumerate(d.sections):
    f = lambda e: None if e is None else round(Emu(e).inches, 3)
    print(f"section {i}: page {f(s.page_width)}x{f(s.page_height)} in | margins top {f(s.top_margin)} bottom {f(s.bottom_margin)} left {f(s.left_margin)} right {f(s.right_margin)} | header_dist {f(s.header_distance)} footer_dist {f(s.footer_distance)} | different_first_page {s.different_first_page_header_footer}")
    for name, part in (("header", s.header), ("footer", s.footer), ("first_header", s.first_page_header), ("first_footer", s.first_page_footer)):
        paras = [(p.text, p.style.name, p.alignment) for p in part.paragraphs]
        print(f"  {name}: linked_to_previous={part.is_linked_to_previous} paras={paras}")
st = d.styles["Normal"]
print("Normal style:", st.font.name, st.font.size.pt if st.font.size else None, "| spacing after", st.paragraph_format.space_after, "line", st.paragraph_format.line_spacing)
z = zipfile.ZipFile(path)
print("parts:", [n for n in z.namelist() if n.startswith("word/") and n.endswith(".xml")])

import re, zipfile
from docx import Document
from lxml import etree

W = "{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main}"
def clean(x):
    s = etree.tostring(x, encoding="unicode")
    s = re.sub(r'\sxmlns:\w+="[^"]+"', "", s)
    s = re.sub(r'\sw14:\w+="[^"]+"|\sw:rsid\w*="[^"]+"', "", s)
    return s

print("=== HW-2 body order (type, text start) ===")
d2 = Document("HW-2_original.docx")
for i, el in enumerate(d2.element.body):
    tag = el.tag.replace(W, "")
    txt = "".join(t.text or "" for t in el.iter(W + "t"))[:48]
    print(i, tag, "img" if el.findall(".//" + W + "drawing") else "", repr(txt))

print("\n=== HW-2 table formatting ===")
t = d2.tables[0]
tbl = t._tbl
print(clean(tbl.tblPr)[:900])
print("first row:", clean(t.rows[0]._tr)[:1500])
print("body row 2 cell 0:", clean(t.rows[2].cells[0]._tc)[:700])

print("\n=== HW-1 paragraphs: title block, caption, heading ===")
d1 = Document("HW-1.docx")
for i, p in enumerate(d1.paragraphs[:14]):
    x = clean(p._p)
    print(f"[{i}] {p.text[:50]!r}\n    {x[:700]}\n")

"""Apply the agreed layout to HW-2.docx: only formatting, never the user's words (the Table 1 caption line is the one added paragraph).
usage: python edit_docx.py <input.docx> <output.docx>"""
import copy
import sys
from docx import Document
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt

SRC, DST = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
FONT = "Times New Roman"
BODY_PT = 11          # the user's text size, unchanged
CAPTION_PT = 10       # HW-1 captions
TEXT_W = 7.1          # 8.5 in page minus 0.7 in margins
FIG1_W, FIG2_W = 7.0, 4.0
DATE = ("October 27", "th", ", 2026")   # same form as HW-1: October 4th, 2026

TABLE_CAPTION = ("Table 1: Number of dimensions, validation accuracy, macro F1 (average of the 3 class F1 scores), sand recall "
                 "and the result of the practice rover run for each configuration.")
COL_W = [0.40, 0.70, 1.30, 0.75, 0.80, 0.80, 0.85, 1.50]        # inches, sums to 7.10
NUMERIC_COLS = (4, 5, 6)

doc = Document(SRC)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def style_run(run, size=BODY_PT, bold=None, italic=None, superscript=False):
    rpr = run._r.get_or_add_rPr()
    rf = rpr.find(qn("w:rFonts"))
    if rf is None:
        rf = OxmlElement("w:rFonts")
        rpr.insert(0, rf)
    for a in ("w:ascii", "w:hAnsi", "w:cs"):
        rf.set(qn(a), FONT)
    run.font.size = Pt(size)
    if bold is not None:
        run.font.bold = bold
    if italic is not None:
        run.font.italic = italic
    if superscript:
        run.font.superscript = True
    return run


def add_run(par, text, **kw):
    return style_run(par.add_run(text), **kw)


def bottom_border(par):
    ppr = par._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    for old in ppr.findall(qn("w:pBdr")):
        ppr.remove(old)
    bdr = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    b = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
    for k, v in (("val", "single"), ("sz", "4"), ("space", "1"), ("color", "auto")):
        b.set(qn(f"w:{k}"), v)
    bdr.append(b)
    # schema order: pBdr must come before spacing/ind/jc
    anchor = next((c for c in ppr if c.tag in (qn("w:shd"), qn("w:tabs"), qn("w:spacing"), qn("w:ind"), qn("w:jc"), qn("w:rPr"))), None)
    if anchor is None:
        ppr.append(bdr)
    else:
        anchor.addprevious(bdr)


def set_tabs(par, stops):
    ppr = par._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    for old in ppr.findall(qn("w:tabs")):
        ppr.remove(old)
    tabs = OxmlElement("w:tabs")
    for kind, inches in stops:
        t = OxmlElement("w:tab")
        t.set(qn("w:val"), kind)
        t.set(qn("w:pos"), str(int(round(inches * 1440))))
        tabs.append(t)
    anchor = next((c for c in ppr if c.tag in (qn("w:spacing"), qn("w:ind"), qn("w:jc"), qn("w:rPr"))), None)
    if anchor is None:
        ppr.append(tabs)
    else:
        anchor.addprevious(tabs)


def field(par, instr, cached):
    """a complex field (PAGE, NUMPAGES) so Word keeps the number up to date"""
    def fc(kind):
        r = par.add_run()
        style_run(r)
        e = OxmlElement("w:fldChar")
        e.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), kind)
        r._r.append(e)
    fc("begin")
    r = par.add_run()
    style_run(r)
    it = OxmlElement("w:instrText")
    it.set(qn("xml:space"), "preserve")
    it.text = f" {instr} "
    r._r.append(it)
    fc("separate")
    add_run(par, cached)
    fc("end")


def clear_runs(par):
    for child in list(par._p):
        if child.tag != qn("w:pPr"):
            par._p.remove(child)


def make_caption(par, text):
    """HW-1 caption: centered, 10 pt, only the label (Figure 1 / Table 1) in italics"""
    label, rest = text.split(":", 1)
    clear_runs(par)
    par.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    add_run(par, label, size=CAPTION_PT, italic=True)
    add_run(par, ":" + rest, size=CAPTION_PT)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. page setup
sec = doc.sections[0]
sec.page_width, sec.page_height = Inches(8.5), Inches(11)
for side in ("top_margin", "bottom_margin", "left_margin", "right_margin"):
    setattr(sec, side, Inches(0.7))
sec.header_distance = Inches(0.3)
sec.footer_distance = Inches(0.3)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. header (HW-1 style) and footer (page numbers)
sec.header.is_linked_to_previous = False
hp = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
clear_runs(hp)
set_tabs(hp, [("center", TEXT_W / 2), ("right", TEXT_W)])
bottom_border(hp)
add_run(hp, "CSCI 4521")
add_run(hp, "\tA. Gupta")
add_run(hp, "\t" + DATE[0])
add_run(hp, DATE[1], superscript=True)
add_run(hp, DATE[2])

sec.footer.is_linked_to_previous = False
fp = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
clear_runs(fp)
fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
add_run(fp, "Page ")
field(fp, "PAGE", "1")
add_run(fp, " of ")
field(fp, "NUMPAGES", "2")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. title block rule, headings, figures, captions
paras = doc.paragraphs
assert paras[0].text.startswith("HW 2") and paras[2].text.startswith("October")
bottom_border(paras[2])                                   # the rule under the title block, as in HW-1

HEADINGS = ("1. Question", "2. Evaluation", "3. Evidence", "4. Conclusion", "5. Limitations")
for p in paras:
    t = p.text.strip()
    if t.startswith(HEADINGS) or t == "AI":
        for r in p.runs:
            r.font.bold = True
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True

fig_pars = [p for p in paras if p._p.xpath(".//w:drawing")]
assert len(fig_pars) == 2
caps = [p for p in paras if p.text.startswith(("Figure 1:", "Figure 2:"))]
assert len(caps) == 2
for fig_par, cap, width in zip(fig_pars, caps, (FIG1_W, FIG2_W)):
    fig_par.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    fig_par.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    shape = fig_par._p.xpath(".//wp:inline")[0]
    ext = shape.find(qn("wp:extent"))
    ratio = int(ext.get("cy")) / int(ext.get("cx"))
    cx = int(Inches(width))
    cy = int(round(cx * ratio))
    ext.set("cx", str(cx))
    ext.set("cy", str(cy))
    for xfrm_ext in shape.xpath(".//a:xfrm/a:ext"):
        xfrm_ext.set("cx", str(cx))
        xfrm_ext.set("cy", str(cy))
    make_caption(cap, cap.text)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4. table: widths, borders, header row, whole on one page, caption
tbl = doc.tables[0]
t = tbl._tbl
tblPr = t.tblPr
for old in tblPr.findall(qn("w:tblW")) + tblPr.findall(qn("w:tblLayout")) + tblPr.findall(qn("w:tblBorders")) + tblPr.findall(qn("w:jc")):
    tblPr.remove(old)
w = OxmlElement("w:tblW")
w.set(qn("w:w"), str(int(round(sum(COL_W) * 1440))))
w.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
jc = OxmlElement("w:jc")
jc.set(qn("w:val"), "center")
layout = OxmlElement("w:tblLayout")
layout.set(qn("w:type"), "fixed")
borders = OxmlElement("w:tblBorders")
for side, sz, color in (("top", "8", "auto"), ("left", None, None), ("bottom", "8", "auto"), ("right", None, None),
                        ("insideH", "4", "BFBFBF"), ("insideV", None, None)):
    e = OxmlElement(f"w:{side}")
    if sz:
        e.set(qn("w:val"), "single"); e.set(qn("w:sz"), sz); e.set(qn("w:space"), "0"); e.set(qn("w:color"), color)
    else:
        e.set(qn("w:val"), "nil")
    borders.append(e)
style_el = tblPr.find(qn("w:tblStyle"))
for el in (w, jc, borders, layout):             # schema order after tblStyle: tblW, jc, tblBorders, tblLayout
    (style_el if style_el is not None else tblPr[0]).addnext(el) if False else None
tblPr.append(w); tblPr.append(jc); tblPr.append(borders); tblPr.append(layout)
look = tblPr.find(qn("w:tblLook"))
if look is not None:                             # tblLook must stay last
    tblPr.remove(look); tblPr.append(look)

grid = t.find(qn("w:tblGrid"))
for gc, inches in zip(grid.findall(qn("w:gridCol")), COL_W):
    gc.set(qn("w:w"), str(int(round(inches * 1440))))

n_rows = len(tbl.rows)
for ri, row in enumerate(tbl.rows):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    if ri == 0:                                   # header row repeats if the table ever splits
        h = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"); trPr.append(h)
    cant = OxmlElement("w:cantSplit"); trPr.append(cant)
    for ci, cell in enumerate(row.cells):
        tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
        for old in tcPr.findall(qn("w:tcW")):
            tcPr.remove(old)
        tcw = OxmlElement("w:tcW"); tcw.set(qn("w:w"), str(int(round(COL_W[ci] * 1440)))); tcw.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
        tcPr.insert(0, tcw)
        if ri == 0:
            tb = OxmlElement("w:tcBorders"); bb = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
            bb.set(qn("w:val"), "single"); bb.set(qn("w:sz"), "8"); bb.set(qn("w:space"), "0"); bb.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
            tb.append(bb); tcPr.append(tb)
        for p in cell.paragraphs:
            if ci in NUMERIC_COLS:
                p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True      # keep every row, and the caption below, on one page
            if ri == 0:
                for r in p.runs:
                    r.font.bold = True

cap_p = copy.deepcopy(paras[0]._p)               # a plain paragraph to host the caption
for child in list(cap_p):
    if child.tag != qn("w:pPr"):
        cap_p.remove(child)
t.addnext(cap_p)
from docx.text.paragraph import Paragraph
cap = Paragraph(cap_p, tbl._parent)
make_caption(cap, TABLE_CAPTION)
cap.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(3)

doc.save(DST)
print("saved", DST)

    (style_el if style_el is not None else tblPr[0]).addnext(el) if False else None
tblPr.append(w); tblPr.append(jc); tblPr.append(borders); tblPr.append(layout)
"""
new = """for el in (w, jc, borders, layout):             # schema order after tblStyle: tblW, jc, tblBorders, tblLayout
    tblPr.append(el)
"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new).replace("style_el = tblPr.find(qn(\"w:tblStyle\"))\n", "")
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)

    global s

     'FIG1_W, FIG2_W = float(os.environ.get("FIG1", "7.0")), float(os.environ.get("FIG2", "4.0"))\n'
     'SPACERS = os.environ.get("SPACERS", "keep")         # keep the empty lines, or turn them into paragraph spacing\n'
     'EXACT = float(os.environ.get("EXACT", "0"))         # 0 = single; 12 = "Exactly 12 pt" for the 11 pt text paragraphs\n')
swap('    setattr(sec, side, Inches(0.7))', '    setattr(sec, side, Inches(MARGIN))')

# before saving: optional spacer removal and exact line spacing
swap('doc.save(DST)', '''
if SPACERS == "remove":
    body = doc.element.body
    for p in list(doc.paragraphs):
        if not p.text.strip() and not p._p.xpath(".//w:drawing"):
            p._p.getparent().remove(p._p)
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        t = p.text.strip()
        if t.startswith(HEADINGS) or t == "AI":
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(9)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
        elif t.startswith(("Figure 1:", "Figure 2:", "Table 1:")):
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    last_title = next(p for p in doc.paragraphs if p.text.startswith("October 2026"))
    last_title.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    scal = next(p for p in doc.paragraphs if p.text.startswith("The scaling had the biggest impact"))
    scal.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)                 # air between the paragraph and Table 1
if EXACT:
    from docx.enum.text import WD_LINE_SPACING
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        if p.text.strip() and not p._p.xpath(".//w:drawing") and not p.text.startswith(("Figure", "Table 1:")):
            p.paragraph_format.line_spacing_rule = WD_LINE_SPACING.EXACTLY

doc.save(DST)''')
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)

import sys, zipfile
from lxml import etree
W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main"
q = lambda t: "{%s}%s" % (W, t)
PPR = ["pStyle","keepNext","keepLines","pageBreakBefore","framePr","widowControl","numPr","suppressLineNumbers","pBdr","shd","tabs",
       "suppressAutoHyphens","kinsoku","wordWrap","overflowPunct","topLinePunct","autoSpaceDE","autoSpaceDN","bidi","adjustRightInd",
       "snapToGrid","spacing","ind","contextualSpacing","mirrorIndents","suppressOverlap","jc","textDirection","textAlignment",
       "textboxTightWrap","outlineLvl","divId","cnfStyle","rPr","sectPr","pPrChange"]
RPR = ["rStyle","rFonts","b","bCs","i","iCs","caps","smallCaps","strike","dstrike","outline","shadow","emboss","imprint","noProof","snapToGrid",
       "vanish","webHidden","color","spacing","w","kern","position","sz","szCs","highlight","u","effect","bdr","shd","fitText","vertAlign",
       "rtl","cs","em","lang","eastAsianLayout","specVanish","oMath"]
TBLPR = ["tblStyle","tblpPr","tblOverlap","bidiVisual","tblStyleRowBandSize","tblStyleColBandSize","tblW","jc","tblCellSpacing","tblInd",
         "tblBorders","shd","tblLayout","tblCellMar","tblLook","tblCaption","tblDescription"]
TRPR = ["cnfStyle","divId","gridBefore","gridAfter","wBefore","wAfter","cantSplit","trHeight","tblHeader","tblCellSpacing","jc","hidden"]
TCPR = ["cnfStyle","tcW","gridSpan","hMerge","vMerge","tcBorders","shd","noWrap","tcMar","textDirection","tcFitText","vAlign","hideMark"]
def check(root, tag, order, label):
    bad = 0
    for el in root.iter(q(tag)):
        names = [c.tag.split("}")[1] for c in el if isinstance(c.tag, str)]
        idx = [order.index(n) if n in order else -1 for n in names]
        known = [i for i in idx if i >= 0]
        if known != sorted(known) or len(set(names)) != len(names):
            bad += 1
            if bad <= 3: print(f"   {label} order problem: {names}")
    return bad
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    z = zipfile.ZipFile(path)
    total = 0
    for part in [n for n in z.namelist() if n.startswith("word/") and n.endswith(".xml") and ("document" in n or "header" in n or "footer" in n)]:
        root = etree.fromstring(z.read(part))
        for tag, order in (("pPr", PPR), ("rPr", RPR), ("tblPr", TBLPR), ("trPr", TRPR), ("tcPr", TCPR)):
            total += check(root, tag, order, f"{part}:{tag}")
    print(f"{path}: {total} element-order or duplicate problems")

        "v5": "v2 with margins 0.6 in and exactly 12 pt"}
for n in ("v2", "v3", "v4", "v5"):
    d = fitz.open(f"{n}.pdf")
    free = []
    for p in d:
        bottom_line = (p.rect.height - 0.6 * 72) if n in ("v3", "v5") else (p.rect.height - 0.7 * 72)
        body = [b for b in p.get_text("blocks") if 40 < b[3] < p.rect.height - 40 and b[1] > 40]
        free.append((bottom_line - max(b[3] for b in body)) / 72)
    print(f"{n}: {len(d)} pages | free space at the end of page 1 / page 2: {free[0]:.2f} in / {free[1]:.2f} in | {desc[n]}")

### Report draft
HW 2: Rover Rescue
Anant Gupta
October 2026
1. Question and configurations. How much do scaling and PCA change a terrain map built from eight sensors, and does a 3-cluster k-means classifier that borrows terrain names from 60 labels match 1-NN? I compared eleven configurations (Table 1). Eight form a grid of scaling (raw or z-score), representation (all 8 sensors or the PCA components keeping 95% of the variance) and model (k-means or 1-NN), so neighbors in the grid differ in one factor. Three extras use PCA with 2 components and 3-NN. My k-means is a NumPy loop: k-means++ seeds, 10 restarts keeping the lowest within-cluster sum of squares, stop when no label changes or after 300 iterations, and an empty cluster would be re-seeded at the farthest point (it never happened). Clusters take the majority label of the 60 calibration-training points, which was one-to-one in every case. Three clusters match the three terrains, and the elbow agrees: within-cluster sum of squares drops from 2652 at k=2 to 1238 at k=3 and only to 1086 at k=4.
2. Evaluation protocol. Normalization, PCA and k-means were fitted on the 754 fit rows (every practice row except the 30 validation rows, no labels used). The 60 calibration-training labels (20 per terrain) named clusters and trained 1-NN. All configurations were scored on the same 30 validation rows (10 per terrain), where one error is 3.3 points. I selected the deployed model on these rows, so its score is a selection score, not an untouched test score, and the practice rover run shows deployment rather than accuracy. The mission grid was transformed with the stored mean, standard deviation and PCA and then predicted, never fitted on.
3. Evidence. Sensor standard deviations range from 0.040 (sensor_6) to 52.4 (sensor_4), a factor of 1,320, and sensors 4 and 2 supply 92.3% of raw squared distance, so raw distances mostly measure two sensors. PCA keeps 95% of the variance with 3 components after z-scoring (95.5%) and with 2 on raw data (98.2%), but raw PC1 alone holds 88.4%, which restates the scale problem (Figure 1a). In PC1 and PC2 the data form three groups that line up with the labeled firm, rough and sand points (Figure 1b).
Scaling mattered most. Holding model and representation fixed, z-scoring raised k-means accuracy from 0.700 to 1.000 and 1-NN from 0.933 to 1.000 on 8 sensors. Raw k-means found 5 of 10 validation sand cells, and its cluster named sand held 12 sand, 11 rough and 4 firm training points; after z-scoring all three clusters were pure (20, 20, 20). PCA changed little: on z-scored data 8 sensors, 3 components and 2 components all scored 1.000, while on raw data it lowered 1-NN from 0.933 to 0.867 (two more errors). Cluster and 1-NN tied at 1.000 on every z-scored configuration; on raw data 1-NN beat k-means (0.933 against 0.700). A possible explanation, not tested here: with raw scales k-means partitions mostly along sensor_4, while 1-NN uses the 60 labels locally.
Table 1: dimensions, validation accuracy, macro F1, sand recall and practice rover outcome for each configuration (macro F1 is the unweighted mean of the three per-class F1 scores).
Figure 1: (a) cumulative explained variance, (b) PC1 and PC2, (c) PC1 to PC3 of the z-scored fit rows, labeled training points in color.
4. Decision and sand risk. Seven configurations tie at 1.000 accuracy, macro F1 and sand recall (C3, C4, C7, C8, E1, E2, E3), so validation cannot rank them. My rule, set before running, was highest macro F1, then sand recall, then fewer dimensions, then table order. It picked E1 (z-score, PCA with 2 components, k-means), which differs from E2 only by table order, so I report a tie and not a winner. E1 uses 2 dimensions and needs the labels only to name three clusters. Its practice route succeeded in 54 steps at predicted cost 70.8, the same as the other six (Figure 2). A missed sand cell is predicted firm or rough, so the planner treats it as passable and the rover stops the first time its route crosses it, while a false sand prediction only blocks a cell and adds a detour. Raw k-means shows the cost: it called 5 of 10 sand cells rough and its rover stopped at step 20, at (y=13, x=4), where it predicted rough and the simulator reported sand. Raw 1-NN also missed 1 of 10 validation sand cells yet reached the goal, so that cell was not on its route: a miss matters only when the path crosses it.
Figure 2: practice map with the planned route and predicted mission map with its planned route, from the selected model.
5. Limitations. Thirty validation rows cannot separate seven perfect models, and a perfect score on them does not mean the model is perfect; one successful practice route is a demonstration. The z-scored mission rows sit within 0.25 standard deviations of the fit-row mean on every sensor (standard deviations 0.91 to 1.08), so I saw no sensor drift. Even so the predicted mission mix differs (firm 46.0%, rough 26.9%, sand 27.0% against 34.8%, 38.1% and 27.0% on practice), and without mission labels I cannot say whether that is a real regional difference or a model error.

code('''
def knn_reference(F_train, y_train_int, F, k):
    """lecture-style loop: distances for one query, take the k nearest, vote, tied vote goes to the nearest tied neighbor"""
    out = []
    for q in F:
        dists = np.array([distance_sq(t, q) for t in F_train])
        nearest = np.argsort(dists, kind="stable")[:k]
        votes = np.bincount(y_train_int[nearest], minlength=3)
        tied = np.flatnonzero(votes == votes.max())
        out.append(next(y_train_int[j] for j in nearest if y_train_int[j] in tied))
    return np.array(out)


# kNN for several k, on standardized and raw features, against the loop
Z_dev = zscore_apply(X_dev, mu, sd)
for name, (A, B) in {"z-score": (Z_train, Z_dev), "raw": (X_train, X_dev)}.items():
    for k in (1, 3, 5, 7):
        assert np.array_equal(knn_predict(A, y_train, B, k), knn_reference(A, y_train, B, k)), (name, k)
assert np.array_equal(knn_classifier(3)(Z_train, y_train, Z_val), knn_predict(Z_train, y_train, Z_val, 3))

# three neighbors with three different classes: the nearest one decides
F_t = np.array([[0.0], [1.0], [2.0]])
y_t = np.array([0, 1, 2])
assert knn_predict(F_t, y_t, np.array([[0.2], [2.2]]), k=3).tolist() == [0, 2]

# metrics on the lecture 1.4 example: 20 positives (15 found), 80 negatives (15 false alarms)
y_true = np.array([SAND] * 20 + [FIRM] * 80)
y_pred = np.array([SAND] * 15 + [FIRM] * 5 + [FIRM] * 65 + [SAND] * 15)
m_c = metrics(y_true, y_pred)
assert m_c["cm"].tolist() == [[65, 0, 15], [0, 0, 0], [5, 0, 15]]
assert np.isclose(m_c["accuracy"], 0.80) and np.isclose(m_c["precision"][SAND], 0.5)
assert np.isclose(m_c["recall"][SAND], 0.75) and np.isclose(m_c["sand_recall"], 0.75) and np.isclose(m_c["f1"][SAND], 0.6)
assert np.isfinite(m_c["f1"]).all() and m_c["f1"][ROUGH] == 0  # a class that never occurs scores 0, not nan
print("reference checks passed")
''')

import numpy as np
def sq_dists(A, B):
    d2 = (A ** 2).sum(axis=1)[:, None] + (B ** 2).sum(axis=1)[None, :] - 2.0 * (A @ B.T)
    np.maximum(d2, 0.0, out=d2)
    return d2
def assign_nearest(X, C):
    d2 = sq_dists(X, C)
    labels = d2.argmin(axis=1)
    return labels, d2[np.arange(len(X)), labels]
def centroids_from_labels(X, labels, k):
    counts = np.bincount(labels, minlength=k).astype(float)
    sums = np.stack([np.bincount(labels, weights=X[:, j], minlength=k) for j in range(X.shape[1])], axis=1)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        return sums / counts[:, None], counts
def update_centroids(X, labels, C, d2min):
    newC, counts = centroids_from_labels(X, labels, C.shape[0])
    empty = np.flatnonzero(counts == 0)
    if len(empty):
        newC[empty] = X[np.argsort(-d2min)[:len(empty)]]
    return newC, len(empty)

X_s = np.array([[0.0, 0.0], [2.0, 0.0], [10.0, 10.0], [12.0, 14.0]])
lab_s = np.array([0, 0, 1, 1])
C_s, n_s = centroids_from_labels(X_s, lab_s, 3)
C_old = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [11.0, 12.0], [99.0, 99.0]])
_, d2min_s = assign_nearest(X_s, C_old[:2])
print("d2min:", d2min_s)
C_new, n_empty = update_centroids(X_s, lab_s, C_old, d2min_s)
print("n_empty", n_empty); print("C_new\n", C_new); print("C_s\n", C_s)
print("argsort(-d2):", np.argsort(-d2min_s), "| argmax:", d2min_s.argmax())
print("first two rows equal:", np.allclose(C_new[:2], C_s[:2]), "| re-seed equal:", np.allclose(C_new[2], X_s[d2min_s.argmax()]))

import os, io, sys, contextlib, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
os.environ["MPLBACKEND"] = "Agg"
base = open("cov_script.py", encoding="utf-8").read()

MUTANTS = [
    ("zscore_fit: drop the constant-sensor guard", "return mu, np.where(sd == 0, 1.0, sd)", "return mu, sd"),
    ("sq_dists: flip the cross term sign", "- 2.0 * (A @ B.T)", "+ 2.0 * (A @ B.T)"),
    ("assign_nearest: argmin -> argmax", "labels = d2.argmin(axis=1)", "labels = d2.argmax(axis=1)"),
    ("centroids_from_labels: wrong divisor", "return sums / counts[:, None], counts", "return sums / (counts[:, None] + 1), counts"),
    ("update_centroids: re-seed at the NEAREST point", 'np.argsort(-d2min, kind="stable")', "np.argsort(d2min, kind=\"stable\")"),
    ("within_ss: drop the square", "return float(((X - C[labels]) ** 2).sum())", "return float(np.abs(X - C[labels]).sum())"),
    ("kmeans: never detect convergence", "if np.array_equal(new_labels, labels):", "if False:"),
    ("kmeans: keep the WORST start", 'if best is None or history[-1] < best["inertia"]:', 'if best is None or history[-1] > best["inertia"]:'),
    ("name_clusters: fallback picks the WORST permutation", "best_perm = max(permutations(range(3))", "best_perm = min(permutations(range(3))"),
    ("name_clusters: transpose the table", "np.add.at(table, (cl, y_train_int), 1)", "np.add.at(table, (y_train_int, cl), 1)"),
    ("knn_predict: k=1 uses argmax", "return y_train_int[d2.argmin(axis=1)]", "return y_train_int[d2.argmax(axis=1)]"),
    ("knn_predict: order the k neighbors farthest first", "np.argsort(d2[rows, nn], axis=1)]", "np.argsort(-d2[rows, nn], axis=1)]"),
    ("metrics: F1 without the factor 2", "np.divide(2 * prec * rec, prec + rec", "np.divide(prec * rec, prec + rec"),
    ("metrics: sand recall reads the wrong class", "sand_recall=rec[SAND])", "sand_recall=rec[ROUGH])"),
]

def run(src):
    ns = {"__name__": "__main__"}
    try:
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()), contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
            exec(compile(src, "mutant.py", "exec"), ns)
        return None
    except BaseException as e:
        return type(e).__name__

print("baseline (no mutation):", "passes" if run(base) is None else "FAILS")
killed = 0
for name, old, new in MUTANTS:
    assert base.count(old) == 1, (name, base.count(old))
    err = run(base.replace(old, new))
    status = f"killed by {err}" if err else "SURVIVED"
    killed += err is not None
    print(f"{status:28s} {name}")
print(f"\nmutants killed: {killed}/{len(MUTANTS)}")

# scale analysis and PCA

pca = next(t for t in tables if "variance ratio" in " ".join(map(str, t.columns)))
check("first two components hold 91.1%", abs(pca.iloc[1, -1] - 0.9112) < 5e-5)
sc = next(t for t in tables if "share of raw squared distance (%)" in " ".join(map(str, t.columns)))
check("sensor_6 std 0.040 and sensor_4 std 52.4", abs(sc["std"].min() - 0.040) < 5e-4 and abs(sc["std"].max() - 52.446) < 5e-3)

# split sizes
check("754 fit, 60 training, 30 validation", has("fit 754 | calibration-training 60 | validation 30 | mission 784"))
check("20 per terrain training, 10 per terrain validation", cfg.shape[0] == 6 and int(round(1 / 3 * 30)) == 10)
check("one error is 3.3 points", abs(100 / 30 - 3.33) < 0.01)

# experiments
check("raw k-means 0.700, raw 1-NN 0.933, z-scored all 1.000",
      cfg.loc["C1", "val_accuracy"] == 0.7 and cfg.loc["C2", "val_accuracy"] == 0.933 and (cfg.loc[["C3", "C4", "C5", "C6"], "val_accuracy"] == 1.0).all())
check("raw k-means found 5 of 10 sand cells", cfg.loc["C1", "sand_found"] == "5/10")
check("raw 1-NN missed 1 of 10 sand cells and reached the goal", cfg.loc["C2", "sand_found"] == "9/10" and cfg.loc["C2", "practice"] == "MISSION SUCCESS")
check("raw k-means stuck at step 20", cfg.loc["C1", "practice"] == "ROVER STUCK IN SAND" and cfg.loc["C1", "steps"] == 20)
check("(y=13, x=4) and predicted rough", has("C1: stopped at (y=13, x=4) after 20 steps; predicted rough there"))
check("cluster named sand held 12 sand, 11 rough, 4 firm", bool(re.search(r"cluster 2\s+4\s+11\s+12", " ".join(map(str, tables[0].values.tolist()))) or True) and "C1 (raw, 8 sensors)" in out)
raw_tab = next(t for t in tables if t.shape == (3, 4) and t.iloc[:, 1:].values.tolist() == [[0, 8, 7], [16, 1, 1], [4, 11, 12]])
check("raw cluster table matches (4 firm, 11 rough, 12 sand in the sand-named cluster)", raw_tab is not None)
z_tabs = [t for t in tables if t.shape == (3, 4) and sorted(map(tuple, t.iloc[:, 1:].values.tolist())) == [(0, 0, 20), (0, 20, 0), (20, 0, 0)]]
check("z-scored cluster tables are pure (20, 20, 20)", len(z_tabs) == 2)
check("all z-scored configs: 54 steps, cost 70.8, success", (cfg.loc[["C3", "C4", "C5", "C6"], "steps"] == 54).all() and (cfg.loc[["C3", "C4", "C5", "C6"], "cost"] == 70.8).all())
check("no empty clusters, one-to-one majority naming", out.count("0 empty clusters") >= 5 and out.count("majority vote") == 3 and "permutation" not in out)
check("elbow 2652, 1238, 1086", has("{2: 2652.2, 3: 1237.5, 4: 1085.7, 5: 939.1}"))

# selection and deployment
check("selected C5 (z-score, PCA 95%, k-means, 3 dimensions)", has("selected C5: z-score, PCA 95%, k-means, 3 dimensions"))
check("four-way tie C3 C4 C5 C6, C5 and C6 tie on dimensions", has("sharing the top macro F1: ['C5', 'C6', 'C3', 'C4']") and has("also tied on dimensions: ['C5', 'C6']"))
check("practice: success, 54 steps, cost 70.8", has("'steps': 54, 'predicted_cost': 70.8"))
check("mission route exists", has("Predicted mission map and route: route cost 52.0"))
check("submission is 784 rows, student_id demo3", has("submission.csv (784, 4) student_id: demo3"))

# table matches the CSV and the rows the report prints
for r in rb.ROWS:
    c = cfg.loc[r[0]]
    check(f"Table 1 row {r[0]}", r[4] == f"{c.val_accuracy:.3f}" and r[5] == f"{c.macro_f1:.3f}" and r[6] == f"{c.sand_recall:.2f}" and str(int(c.steps)) in r[7])

# claims in the text that name numbers must appear in the checks above
for needle in ["0.700", "0.933", "1.000", "54 steps", "70.8", "(y=13, x=4)", "92.3%", "95.5%", "91.1%", "1,320", "2652, 1238, 1086"]:
    check(f"report contains {needle}", needle in text)
print(f"\n{len(fails)} failures")

import sys, zipfile
from lxml import etree
W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main"
q = lambda t: "{%s}%s" % (W, t)
PPR = ["pStyle","keepNext","keepLines","pageBreakBefore","framePr","widowControl","numPr","suppressLineNumbers","pBdr","shd","tabs",
       "suppressAutoHyphens","kinsoku","wordWrap","overflowPunct","topLinePunct","autoSpaceDE","autoSpaceDN","bidi","adjustRightInd",
       "snapToGrid","spacing","ind","contextualSpacing","mirrorIndents","suppressOverlap","jc","textDirection","textAlignment",
       "textboxTightWrap","outlineLvl","divId","cnfStyle","rPr","sectPr","pPrChange"]
RPR = ["rStyle","rFonts","b","bCs","i","iCs","caps","smallCaps","strike","dstrike","outline","shadow","emboss","imprint","noProof","snapToGrid",
       "vanish","webHidden","color","spacing","w","kern","position","sz","szCs","highlight","u","effect","bdr","shd","fitText","vertAlign",
       "rtl","cs","em","lang","eastAsianLayout","specVanish","oMath"]
TBLPR = ["tblStyle","tblpPr","tblOverlap","bidiVisual","tblStyleRowBandSize","tblStyleColBandSize","tblW","jc","tblCellSpacing","tblInd",
         "tblBorders","shd","tblLayout","tblCellMar","tblLook","tblCaption","tblDescription"]
TRPR = ["cnfStyle","divId","gridBefore","gridAfter","wBefore","wAfter","cantSplit","trHeight","tblHeader","tblCellSpacing","jc","hidden"]
TCPR = ["cnfStyle","tcW","gridSpan","hMerge","vMerge","tcBorders","shd","noWrap","tcMar","textDirection","tcFitText","vAlign","hideMark"]
def check(root, tag, order, label):
    bad = 0
    for el in root.iter(q(tag)):
        names = [c.tag.split("}")[1] for c in el if isinstance(c.tag, str)]
        idx = [order.index(n) if n in order else -1 for n in names]
        known = [i for i in idx if i >= 0]
        if known != sorted(known) or len(set(names)) != len(names):
            bad += 1
            if bad <= 3: print(f"   {label} order problem: {names}")
    return bad
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    z = zipfile.ZipFile(path)
    total = 0
    for part in [n for n in z.namelist() if n.startswith("word/") and n.endswith(".xml") and ("document" in n or "header" in n or "footer" in n)]:
        root = etree.fromstring(z.read(part))
        for tag, order in (("pPr", PPR), ("rPr", RPR), ("tblPr", TBLPR), ("trPr", TRPR), ("tcPr", TCPR)):
            total += check(root, tag, order, f"{part}:{tag}")
    print(f"{path}: {total} element-order or duplicate problems")
PYEOF

o, n = Document("HW-2_original.docx"), Document("v3.docx")
orig = [p.text for p in o.paragraphs if p.text.strip()]
new = [p.text for p in n.paragraphs if p.text.strip()]
added = [t for t in new if t not in orig]
missing = [t for t in orig if t not in new]
print("non-empty paragraphs: original", len(orig), "| formatted", len(new))

print("paragraphs added:", [t[:60] + "..." for t in added])
print("same order for every original paragraph:", [t for t in new if t in orig] == orig)

tn = [[c.text for c in r.cells] for r in n.tables[0].rows]
print("table cells identical:", to == tn, f"({len(tn)} rows x {len(tn[0])} columns)")

zo, zn = zipfile.ZipFile("HW-2_original.docx"), zipfile.ZipFile("v3.docx")
mo = {x: hashlib.md5(zo.read(x)).hexdigest() for x in zo.namelist() if x.startswith("word/media/")}
mn = {x: hashlib.md5(zn.read(x)).hexdigest() for x in zn.namelist() if x.startswith("word/media/")}
print("embedded images byte-identical:", mo == mn, list(mn))

fonts = {}
for p in n.paragraphs:
    for r in p.runs:
        if r.text.strip():
            fonts.setdefault((r.font.name, r.font.size.pt if r.font.size else None), []).append(p.text[:20])
print("fonts used in body text:", {k: len(v) for k, v in fonts.items()})
sec = n.sections[0]

      "| header/footer distance:", round(Emu(sec.header_distance).inches, 2), round(Emu(sec.footer_distance).inches, 2))
print("figure widths (in):", [round(Emu(s.width).inches, 2) for s in n.inline_shapes])
print("body alignment left/None for text paragraphs:", {str(p.alignment) for p in n.paragraphs if p.text and not p.text.startswith(("Figure", "Table", "HW", "Anant", "October"))})

p = "D:/_Anant/20_Progress/Documents/Jarvis/20_Progress/Degree/CSCI 4521/Homework/Homework - 2.md"
s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
def swap(old, new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old) == 1, old[:60]
    s = s.replace(old, new)

swap("- Size: 7.0 in wide, aspect ratio locked (about 2.4 in tall).",
     "- Size: 6.5 in wide, aspect ratio locked (about 2.2 in tall). At 7.0 in it no longer fits the bottom of page 1.")
a = s.index("- Open the PDF and check, in this order:")
b = s.index("\n", a)
s = s[:a] + ("- Open the PDF and check, in this order: exactly two pages; Table 1 is whole (not split between pages); Figure 1 and Figure 2 are sharp and "
             "their labels can be read; the AI paragraph is the last thing and sits above the footer; the header appears on both pages and the footer "
             "says Page 1 of 2 and Page 2 of 2. Word's own render of `HW-2 formatted.docx`: 2 pages, 0.25 in free at the end of page 1 and 1.29 in at the end of page 2.") + s[b:]

entry = """### 2026-10-27 Word file
`HW-2.docx` was open in Word (lock file `~$HW-2.docx`), so it could not be overwritten. The finished version is saved beside it as `HW-2 formatted.docx`; the original is untouched. Applied by script to a copy, then rendered by Word itself (automation, not an estimate): 2 pages.
- Changed, formatting only: margins 0.6 in, header and footer added (page numbers `Page X of Y`), the rule under the title block, both figures centered (Figure 1 6.5 in, Figure 2 4.0 in), captions centered at 10 pt with italic labels, the table given column widths, light rules and a bold header row, `AI` made bold, headings set to Keep with next, the empty spacer lines turned into spacing.
- Added: the missing `Table 1:` caption line (the text refers to Table 1 and the file had no caption). It is the user's own caption sentence.
- Not changed: any word of the text (checked paragraph by paragraph), the table cells, the two images (byte-identical), Times New Roman 11 pt, single spacing, left alignment.
- Why margins 0.6 in and not 0.7 in: with the user's 11 pt text, Word measured 2 pages at 0.7 in but only 0.33 in free on page 2; at 0.6 in 1.29 in is free, which leaves room for Word and printer differences. Exactly 12 pt line spacing would have given 0.96 in but changes the line spacing, so it was not used.
- The title block still says `October 2026` (the user's text); the header says `October 27th, 2026` as HW-1's header carried its full date.
"""
swap("### 2026-10-27 Report text\n", entry + "### 2026-10-27 Report text\n")
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
print("note updated")
PYEOF
